title: CO2 Monitoring, Compressed-Gas Safety & Authority Boundaries

content.overview: Carbon dioxide may be used in controlled environments, but it is also an odorless asphyxiation hazard and compressed-gas system. Worker safety, alarms, ventilation, access controls and qualified service take priority over crop-enrichment goals.

vocabulary.definition: A condition in which breathing safety can be compromised by oxygen displacement or high gas concentration.
Cylinders, bulk tanks, piping, regulators and associated equipment containing gas under pressure.
A safety alarm intended to trigger protective action rather than routine crop-control optimization.

sections.title: Worker limits are not crop targets
sections.body: OSHA and NIOSH occupational exposure values exist for worker protection and must never be interpreted as recommended enrichment concentrations for cultivation.

sections.title: Alarm means follow the emergency procedure
sections.body: A CO2 life-safety alarm or suspected leak requires the posted emergency response and qualified investigation. Do not enter an unsafe room merely to inspect a controller.

sections.title: Gas-system service is qualified work
sections.body: Cylinder handling, piping, regulator service, leak repair and system modification remain controlled by facility procedure and qualified personnel.

workedExamples: A crop-control dashboard requests CO2 while a life-safety alarm is active; the safety response overrides crop-control optimization.
commonMistakes: Treating exposure limits as enrichment recommendations.
Silencing alarms to protect crop targets.
content.practicalApplication: Review a mock CO2 alarm scenario and document the safe stop and escalation path without entering the hazardous area.
content.summary: CO2 is both a crop-management variable and a worker-safety hazard; safety controls take precedence.
